title: The dormant leg mirrors mainnet's promo slot but not its address book: `local-addresses.ts` still ships a real, funded MockKendu where `mainnet-addresses.ts` ships `Kendu: 0x0`
fingerprintNote: Accepted VERBATIM as supplied by dedup. NOT recomputed by finding-manager. The fingerprint is the only collision-proof key for this record; the label L-xx/Q-xx is run-scoped and collides with run-21 and run-26 labels on this same entry point.
description: With LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false the PhlimboV3 promo slot is genuinely dormant (promoToken 0x0, phase 0, balance 0, rate 0, startPromotion broadcast zero times), which is the mainnet day-one shape and is exactly what run-26 L-03 asked for. But the generated address book is not a mirror: `server/deployments/local-addresses.ts` carries `Kendu: "0x0DCd1Bf9A1b36cE34237eEaFef220932846BCD82"` — a real MockKendu with totalSupply 1.05e24 — whereas the hand-maintained `server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts` carries `Kendu: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"`. So a UI developer on the dormant leg exercises 'dormant promotion on a live token address', while day-one mainnet presents 'dormant promotion on the zero address' — the zero-address handling path is still never rehearsed. Story 079 discloses this in Concerns ('The dormant leg is not a perfect mainnet mirror') and rejected blanking the local Kendu address as out of scope, correctly: the Kendu nudge stream legitimately uses MockKendu and gating it was explicitly forbidden. This is adjacent to, but distinct from, ledger entry 3177eed94ecb6218 (mainnet-addresses.ts carrying type-indistinguishable 0x0 placeholders); dedup should keep them separate — that entry is about the mainnet artifact's ambiguity, this one is about the local leg not reproducing it.
impact: The dormant leg is a faithful mirror of the CONTRACT STATE and a partial mirror of the ENVIRONMENT. The UI's zero-address-token rendering path remains unexercised locally.
attackPath: 1. Not applicable — no adversary and no exploitation route.

2. Miss path only: a UI defect that manifests only when a token address is 0x0 (null render, checksum call on the zero address, unguarded contract read) survives local development because the local environment never presents 0x0, and appears on mainnet day one.
recommendation: Do not blank the local Kendu address — it would break the nudge stream, which legitimately needs MockKendu. Instead give the dormant leg a way to reproduce the zero-address environment without touching the chain: emit `Kendu: "0x0"` into the generated `local-addresses.ts` when `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false` (a change in `server/generate-ts-addresses.js` keyed off the same toggle, not in the Solidity), or add a third UI-side fixture. Either way, amend the dormant-leg log line so it states which parts of the mainnet day-one shape it does and does not reproduce, rather than the current unqualified 'this is the day-one mainnet shape'.
severityRationale: QA is correct. Nothing is broken — the dormant leg delivers precisely what run-26 L-03 asked for, and the residual is disclosed in the story's own Concerns. There is no asset, availability, value or protocol-function impact, and the substance of the record is (a) an environment-fidelity gap on a local rehearsal and (b) a log line that states its mirror claim unqualified. C4 places comment accuracy and this class of completeness observation in QA. It stays recorded rather than dropped so the 'day-one mainnet mirror' claim is not over-read by a future reader.
severityRationaleAsProposed: Proposed QA. The dormant leg delivers exactly what L-03 asked for — a reachable dormant promo state — and this residual is disclosed in the story's own Concerns. It is recorded so the 'day-one mainnet mirror' claim is not over-read, not because anything is broken.

classification.whatActuallyBreaks: Nothing is broken; a mirror is partial. With `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=false` the PhlimboV3 promo slot is genuinely dormant on chain (promoToken 0x0, phase 0, balance 0, rate 0, `startPromotion` broadcast zero times) — exactly what run-26 L-03 asked for. But the generated address book is not a mirror: `server/deployments/local-addresses.ts` carries `Kendu: "0x0DCd1Bf9A1b36cE34237eEaFef220932846BCD82"`, a real MockKendu with totalSupply 1.05e24, whereas the hand-maintained `server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts` carries `Kendu: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"`. So a UI developer on the dormant leg exercises 'dormant promotion on a live token address' while day-one mainnet presents 'dormant promotion on the zero address' — the UI's zero-address-token rendering path is still never rehearsed locally.
classification.whatAnAttackerGains: Nothing. The affected party is a UI developer, and the cost is an unexercised rendering path.
attackPath: 1. Not applicable — no adversary and no exploitation route.

2. Miss path only: a UI defect that manifests only when a token address is 0x0 (null render, checksum call on the zero address, unguarded contract read) survives local development because the local environment never presents 0x0, and appears on mainnet day one.
classification.likelihood: The environment gap is certain; the cost is contingent on the UI having a zero-address-specific defect, which is unmeasured and off this entry point (the UI is not Solidity and its rendering paths were not analysed here).
classification.assumptions: That mainnet ships day one with `Kendu: 0x0`, as the hand-maintained mainnet address book states.
classification.externalRequirements: A zero-address-specific defect in the UI would have to exist for the gap to cost anything.

escalationTrigger: Raise to Low if the UI is shown to have a zero-address-token handling path that actually diverges (a render or read that behaves differently at 0x0 and is not covered by any other fixture) — the gap would then be hiding a real, identified defect class rather than an unexercised branch.
law3: No owner action involved. `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU` is a developer toggle, not an owner privilege, and both of its legs assert.

poc.reason: C4 requires a coded PoC for High/Medium only. Severity here is qa.

Collapsing them would bury the rehearsal-fidelity claim inside an address-book-typing claim and lose it.
